questions.q: A covalent bond is formed when atoms:
questions.explain: Covalent bonds form when non-metal atoms share pairs of electrons.

questions.q: Chlorine gas is identified because it:
questions.explain: Chlorine bleaches damp litmus paper, turning it white.

questions.q: In a flame test, lithium ions give which colour?
questions.explain: Lithium ions produce a crimson flame.

questions.q: Silicon dioxide is an example of a:
questions.explain: Silicon dioxide has a giant covalent (macromolecular) structure.

questions.q: Copper ions produce which colour in a flame test?
questions.explain: Copper ions give a green flame colour.

questions.q: What is one advantage of instrumental methods such as flame emission spectroscopy?
options: They are fast, accurate and use very small samples
questions.explain: Instrumental methods like flame emission spectroscopy are fast, accurate and sensitive, working on tiny samples.
Electrons are transferred from the metal atom to the non-metal atom, forming ions.
Ionic bonds form when a metal transfers electrons to a non-metal.

questions.q: Which test confirms that a gas is hydrogen?
options: It gives a squeaky pop with a lit splint
questions.explain: Hydrogen produces a squeaky pop when a lit splint is held to it.

options: Layers of atoms (ions) can slide over each other
questions.explain: Layers of metal ions slide over one another while the metallic bonding holds them together.

questions.q: When do ionic compounds conduct electricity?
options: When molten or dissolved in water
questions.explain: Ions are only free to move and carry charge when the compound is molten or in solution.

questions.q: When silver nitrate is added to a solution containing iodide ions, the precipitate is:
questions.explain: Iodide ions form a yellow precipitate of silver iodide.
